newsitem.title: UK: IBCA may cut indiviual ratings on six Thai banks.
newsitem.headline: IBCA may cut indiviual ratings on six Thai banks.

text.p: IBCA, the European rating agency said on Thursday it had placed the individual ratings of six major Thai banks on RatingWatch with negative implications.

The banks are; Bangkok Bank currently rated B/C, Krung Thai Bank currently rated C, Thai Farmers Bank currently rated B/C, Siam Commercial Bank currently rated B/C, Bank of Ayudhya currently rated C and Thai Military Bank currently rated C/D.

"This action reflects the state of flux surrounding the Thai economy following the Bank of Thailand's decision on Wednesday to float the baht, and the currency's initial 18 percent depreciation," IBCA said in a statement.

In fax advice to subscribers, IBCA said there were two recent examples which illustrated the contrast in potential impact of a devaluation; - The Hungarian experience, in which a period of austerity, following the devaluation of the forint in 1995, enabled the country to lock in substantial gains in international competitiveness and so provided, within a relatively short period, a sound platform for growth and making Hungary a magnet for direct foreign investment; and - The Mexican experience, in which there was a near-collapse of international investor confidence, leading to a prolonged period of punitive interest rates and dire consequences for the local economy.
"Thailand's situation is more akin to Hungary's than Mexico's," IBCA said. "If that is so, the impact will already have been largely factored into the current individual ratings."
"However, if the situation were to deteriorate more than we expect, we anticipate revising down our ratings."

IBCA said it would continue to monitor the situation closely, paying particular attention to the authorities' ability to maintain Thailand's attractiveness as a recipient of international investment, and the resulting level of domestic interest rates.
